meta.working_title: Every Rank on a Pirate Ship

brief.idea: Climb every rank on a Caribbean pirate ship of 1716, from powder monkey to captain, and learn what each one actually did all day.
brief.angle: Second person: you are the boy, then the sailor, then the officer. Every promotion costs something.
brief.hook_promise: By the end you will know why the captain was the least powerful man aboard in peacetime.

sources.title: Marcus Rediker, Villains of All Nations
Charles Johnson, A General History of the Pyrates (1724)

sections.title: Gun drill
sections.vo_direction: quicker, clipped, the rhythm of orders

shots.vo: Then one morning the drum beats to quarters, and for the first time the drill is not a drill.

image.prompt: the full length of the gun deck from the stern looking forward, every gun run out, crews frozen mid-motion, hatches open above

sfx.prompt: a single drum beating fast, men shouting, feet on planks

shots.vo: Sponge. Load. Ram. Prime. You do not fire the gun. You keep it fed, and you keep your head below the rail.

image.prompt: crouches beside a gun carriage passing a cartridge up to a bare-chested loader, the gun captain above them with the slow match raised

shots.vo: The gun goes off eighteen inches from your ear. You will not hear properly again until Sunday.

image.prompt: flinches away from the gun with both hands clamped over his ears, mouth open, smoke pouring past him toward the open port

shots.vo: And then you run again. Because the gun is empty, and the magazine is not, and that is the whole of your rank.

image.prompt: seen from behind, a small figure disappearing down a smoke-filled ladderway, the gun deck chaos above him going out of view

shots.vo: You are not a sailor yet. You are the thing that keeps the sailors' guns alive.

image.prompt: stands alone on the empty gun deck after the action, cartridge case at his feet, looking down the row of silent guns

sfx.prompt: ringing silence, distant water dripping, a rope creaks once

concepts.prompt: a small boy with a cartridge case looks up at a towering gun deck, viewed from below
a ladder of ranks drawn as ship decks stacked on top of each other, the boy at the bottom

titles: Every Rank on a Pirate Ship (1716)
You Are Eleven and Your Job Is Gunpowder
From Powder Monkey to Captain: Every Rank Explained
publish.description: Climb every rank on a Caribbean pirate ship of 1716. What each rank did, what it paid, and what it cost.

facts.claim: Felt curtains were used at magazine doors specifically to catch sparks.
